setup: Lie on your side on a bench or mat
Light dumbbell in the top hand
Elbow bent to 90°, pinned to your side
Rolled towel between elbow and ribs
execution: Rotate the dumbbell up toward the ceiling
Keep the elbow on your side
faults: Don't lift the elbow off your side

notes: Use a light dumbbell. The cuff muscles are small; heavy loads make the elbow and trunk cheat.
Go only as high as you can with the elbow still on your side.
Load is the one dumbbell; reps are per arm.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain in the shoulder that builds during the set
Numbness or tingling in the arm

regressions.name: No-weight side-lying rotation
regressions.reason: Learn the range with the arm's weight only.

progressions.name: Slow lowering
progressions.reason: A 3-second lowering adds work without more weight.

substitutions.name: Band external rotation
substitutions.reason: Same rotation standing with a band; good for warm-ups and travel.

substitutions.name: Cable external rotation
substitutions.reason: Standing on a stack; easy to load in small steps.

substitutions.name: Face pull
substitutions.reason: Rear-shoulder and upper-back pull with an outward rotation at the end.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Camera at bench height looking at the figure's front as it lies on its side, head to the left. Shows the forearm swinging up like a gate while the upper arm stays on the ribs.

keyPositions.label: Start
keyPositions.describe: Lying on the side, bottom arm under the head. Top elbow bent to 90° and resting on the ribs with a towel, forearm across the stomach holding a light dumbbell.

keyPositions.label: Top
keyPositions.describe: Forearm rotated up toward the ceiling, elbow still on the ribs and bent to 90°. Body has not rolled back.

ikHints: Upper elbow fixed on the side of the ribs
Torso stays still on the bench

uncertain.note: The main muscles are the rotator cuff (infraspinatus, teres minor). The vocabulary has no 'rotator_cuff' word (research Q1), so 'rear_delts' is used as the nearest word. This overstates the rear-delt role.
Mapped to 'horizontal_pull' (rear-shoulder work); no rotation or prehab pattern exists.
'front' here means the camera faces the front of the lying figure. The guide-maker may prefer a different framing.
Approximate drawing targets, not measured data.
